purpose: Adds a settings toggle that overrides WP 7.1+ client-side MIME type handling and refactors encode-quality resolution to use core's size-aware wp_get_image_encode_quality() with safe fallbacks for older cores.
riskRationale: The MIME toggle is well-gated and defaults OFF, but the refactor of LQIP quality introduces a behavioral regression on WP 6.7–7.0 (the current, common cores) that enlarges placeholder payloads; no security concerns found.

text: The MIME-toggle work is clean, well-gated, and thoroughly tested, and routing convert_image() quality through a size-aware helper with a null-guarded fallback is a real improvement over the prior (int) null cast-to-0 bug. However, applying the same quality-resolution helper to generate_lqip() changes LQIP encoding from a deliberate fixed quality 40 to the site's full JPEG quality (~82) on WP 6.7–7.0, silently inflating every placeholder data URI — a regression the PR's own '(default still 40)' claim contradicts.

reasoning: LQIP thumbnails are intentionally low-quality placeholders; using core-quality resolution for them on WP 6.7–7.0 encodes at ~82 instead of 40, roughly doubling base64 placeholder size on every lazy-loaded image. This must be fixed before merge.

message: The client_side_supported_mime_types filter is correctly gated on both the core function existing (WP 7.1+) and the admin toggle being enabled, so older cores and default-OFF installs see zero behavior change. The callback also degrades gracefully to core's list when the stored value is empty/non-array.

resolve_encode_quality() is a solid layered fallback (size-aware helper → flat wp_image_quality() → plugin fallback) and fixes the latent bug where (int) wp_image_quality() cast null to 0, which would have encoded images at quality 0 on WP 6.7–7.0 when no quality was registered for a MIME.

Passing the LQIP thumbnail through resolve_encode_quality('image/jpeg', 40, [w,h]) makes the encode quality follow core on WP 6.7–7.0, where wp_image_quality('image/jpeg') returns the site's full JPEG quality (~82) rather than the intended LQIP quality of 40. LQIP is deliberately a low-quality 20px placeholder; there is no '40 default' on those cores because resolve_encode_quality() prefers core's non-null value. In practice this roughly doubles the size of the base64 placeholder data-URI embedded in every lazy-loaded image, directly contradicting the PR's '(default still 40)' claim and hurting the plugin's core performance goal. The size-aware helper is appropriate for convert_image() output, but not for the placeholder path.
suggestion: Keep the fixed quality 40 for the LQIP encode instead of routing it through core-quality resolution, since placeholder size is intentional and core's per-MIME/per-size quality is meant for full images.

message: The default clientSideMimeTypes array (lines 44–50) is byte-for-byte identical to the DEFAULT_CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_TYPES constant (lines 87–93). The two will drift if core's default formats change, and the duplication is needless. Use the constant in the defaults so there is a single source of truth.
suggestion: Replace the inline literal at lines 44–50 with DEFAULT_CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_TYPES by hoisting the constant (and CLIENT_SIDE_MIME_OPTIONS) above defaultSettings, then referencing it in defaultSettings.

message: The render path calls settings.clientSideMimeTypes.includes( option.value ) (lines 602 and 613) without an Array.isArray guard, unlike toggleClientSideMimeType() which guards defensively (line 114). If settings.clientSideMimeTypes is ever a non-array (e.g. a corrupted/stored string overriding the default via the options spread), .includes would throw a TypeError and crash the tab. The toggle handler treats this case as an empty selection, but the render path assumes an array.
suggestion: Guard the render access, e.g. const mimeList = Array.isArray( settings.clientSideMimeTypes ) ? settings.clientSideMimeTypes : []; then use mimeList.includes( option.value ) in both the chip class and checkbox checked logic.
suggestionCode:
const list = Array.isArray( settings.clientSideMimeTypes ) ? settings.clientSideMimeTypes : [];
// then: list.includes( option.value ) in className and checked
